method: Dates are Git committer dates in each commit’s recorded timezone, not release or download dates. Every available commit subject in the pinned intervals was reviewed; summaries group related base-game changes, with source and patch checks for compatibility and controls. This is a source-history review, not a new gameplay test. The 5 November continuation reviewed only the 12 later wiki changes through 9017e34; the 8 November continuation adds the 35 wiki changes after it through ec84c2d3; a later 8 November follow-up adds the 23 wiki changes after that through fd7d8b89. The 8 November continuation reviews all 1,768 game changes after the 13 October cutoff through 21d656c2 (1,405 non-merge subjects, with message bodies, file lists and selected patches), checks added features against a clean export of 251b9e46 and 21d656c2, and re-checks every compatibility note there. A later 8 November follow-up reviews the 39 game changes after 21d656c2 through c56a00c4 (subjects, message bodies and the patches of the player-facing ones). The public game history was rewritten after the 13 October review without changing its shape: the same 704 commits, dates and subjects lead to the old cutoff 5856103c, which is 4723e3fc in the current history. Groups through 13 October keep the identifiers recorded at that review; later groups, the new 13 October entries and the new compatibility evidence use current identifiers, and the source range is pinned to the current root f4c9aee8 and c56a00c4 (2,511 commits).
gaps: The game history starts with a large snapshot on 16 August 2026. Earlier development and changes between recorded snapshots cannot be dated more precisely.

There are no tags in either inspected checkout. The public game release endpoint returned 404 during review, so game releases could not be verified. The wiki release endpoint returned an empty list. No release numbers are inferred from package metadata.
Optional content, internal refactors, test-only changes and development plans are omitted. Some recorded days therefore have no entry. Broad early snapshots can only support grouped summaries.
Wiki history begins with the standalone import on 9 October. Older atlas capture dates describe preserved media, not earlier commits in this repository.

The cutoff is explicit below. Later commits are not covered until the next review; this chronology does not refresh the dates or receipts in older guides and galleries. Days with only internal, test, documentation, music-review or optional-content changes have no group; 1–3 November 2026 have no game changes at all.

compatibility.text: At the 13 October review, saves were written as format 29 and formats 10–29 were accepted. Format 28 widened stored block IDs; format 29 stores survival milestones. Re-checked at game revision 251b9e46 (8 November 2026): saves are written as format 40 and formats 10–40 are accepted. Formats 30–40 (16–26 October) add precise positions, weather continuity, plot claims, furniture, the 1024-chunk horizon, hatched animals, carried stock and, in format 40, dropped items. Keep a separate copy of your world before trying an older build: there is no downgrade conversion.
compatibility.publicSummary: Back up your world before trying an older game version. Newer saves may not open in older versions.

compatibility.text: Saves before format 10 predate the half-metre grid and are refused, not converted. Supported saved worlds retain their generator selection; updating the game does not turn an old world into the newest terrain generation. Re-checked at 251b9e46 (8 November 2026): saves before format 10 are still refused, and each world still loads its saved generator.
compatibility.publicSummary: Older worlds keep their original terrain. Very old worlds from before the smaller building grid are not converted.

compatibility.text: At the 13 October review the client and server used protocol 16. Re-checked at game revision 251b9e46 (8 November 2026): protocol 104, raised on 8 November with wall lamps. The handshake and LAN listing accept only an exactly equal protocol number. Protocol and terrain/build checks refuse a mismatched peer, so update the server and every player together. This note makes no claim about public-internet hosting.
compatibility.publicSummary: Use matching game versions on the server and each player’s computer.

compatibility.text: New flat workshops are separate saves. Elevated workshops remain in Worlds as legacy workshops with their builds intact. Move a build through the Blueprint library and check the copy before removing the original. Re-checked at 251b9e46 (8 November 2026): legacy workshops still keep their original plate and builds.
compatibility.publicSummary: Older workshops remain in Worlds with their builds intact. Use blueprints to move a build to a new flat workshop.

compatibility.text: The reviewed blueprint format is version 1 and records blocks by stable name. Doors are excluded from captures. Newer or unknown content can be refused; the world-save format number is not the blueprint format number. Re-checked at 251b9e46 (8 November 2026): still format 1 without door leaves; since 25 October a selection that touches placed furniture is not captured and reports "Furniture (n): use Move or Take up".
compatibility.publicSummary: Blueprints leave out doors and cannot include furniture. A blueprint using unsupported blocks may not load.

periods.title: Beds, cooking stove, lamps, lantern light, animal voices and boat sounds

entries.text: Single and double bed plans with a wooden frame and Cream, Sage or Rust wool bedding (single 3 boards + 4 wool, double 6 boards + 7 wool). With the plan put away, right-click a bed to lie down and Space or right-click to get up at a clear, supported exit; a double bed has two places. Resting is only a pose: time and Survival needs carry on and it does not set Home or respawn. It works solo and on servers, where the server confirms the pose, other players see you lying down and two players can share a double bed; occupied beds cannot be moved, changed or taken up.
entries.publicSummary: Added single and double beds with a choice of frame wood and bedding colour. Lie down to rest, alone or on a server, where two players can share a double bed.

entries.text: The Cooking stove plan builds a 1 m stove with wooden feet and a stone or iron body (one board and six stone or raw iron ore). With the plan put away, right-click it, add carried raw meat or venison and charcoal (up to 16 each) and Start one batch; Cancel returns the ingredients. Cooking keeps going while you walk away, is kept through saves and gives no offline progress. It also works on servers and when hosting your own world, where each step waits for the server, and a filled stove must be emptied before taking it up.
entries.publicSummary: Added a cooking stove you build from a furniture plan. Cook raw meat or venison with charcoal, in solo play or on a server.

entries.text: Floor lamp, Table lamp and Wall lamp plans, each costing one red lantern plus two boards in the chosen woods. Lamps start switched on; with the plan put away, right-click with an empty hand to switch one off or on, and the setting is saved with the world. Wall lamps hang on a complete solid wall, and the table lamp stands on solid blocks, not on furniture. Switching also works on servers, where a lamp must be on before it is taken up.
entries.publicSummary: Added floor, table and wall lamps that you switch on and off by hand. They need no fuel and stay as you left them after saving.

entries.text: Red lanterns displayed on tables, desks, bookcases and wall shelves, and lit lamps, now feed the normal nearby-light system, so they light the surrounding walls, floor and ceiling like a placed red lantern. The usual limit of 16 nearby light sources still applies.
entries.publicSummary: Fixed lanterns on furniture not lighting the walls and floor around them.

entries.text: Distant light sources are rejected before their blocks are read when gathering nearby lights, and visible terrain is sorted by cached distance each frame with the same order.
entries.publicSummary: Improved performance when many lights and much terrain are in view.

entries.text: On a server, if another player moved or changed a piece you had locked for a move, the next right-click could place a brand-new piece and spend materials. The move now stays locked and refused ('Source changed | LMB cancels; select again') until you cancel and select the piece again.
entries.publicSummary: Fixed a furniture move on a server turning into a new paid piece when someone else had moved the original first.

entries.text: On a dedicated server, eating while sitting or lying with a blocked way out is refused with 'Make room to stand up before eating' instead of spending the meal without saving it. A host lying in a bed with a blocked exit is no longer refused every other world action, so they can clear the obstruction instead of being stuck until restart.
entries.publicSummary: Fixed meals being lost on a server while lying in a bed with a blocked exit, and the host getting stuck in such a bed.

entries.text: Calls now cover 57 species that plausibly call, up from 25. Hitting one of them plays a short hurt yelp over the shared hit thud, and a fatal blow plays a softer falling sigh. Fish, sharks, jellies, molluscs, crustaceans, insects, snakes, lizards, turtles and quiet mammals such as rabbits and giraffes stay silent.
entries.publicSummary: Added calls for 57 animal species, a short yelp when you hit one and a soft sigh when a blow kills it.

entries.text: Backing up the world you are playing now saves it through the normal checked save first, which also settles a stopped host's recovery record; a direct write could leave that record refusing every later load of the world.
entries.publicSummary: Fixed backing up the open world after hosting it, which could stop that world from loading again.

entries.text: On a server, an open stove re-reads itself once after another furniture change made its view stale, a furniture-move refusal is no longer hidden by background waiting text, and door moves no longer stay blocked after a move whose source was already released.
entries.publicSummary: Fixed an open stove on a server needing to be reopened, move refusals being hidden, and door moves staying blocked.

entries.text: In a single-player world, TNT blasts, artillery shell craters and tank tracks now leave the blocks that hold up placed furniture, as a server blast already did; a tree that holds up furniture is not felled by tracks. Lighting a TNT group by hand is refused with “This TNT cluster touches furniture support” when any piece of the group holds up furniture.
entries.publicSummary: Explosions, shells and tank tracks no longer knock the support out from under placed furniture in single-player worlds.

entries.text: At the helm of the Small sailing boat you now hear a hull rush whose loudness and brightness follow your speed, a sail flutter when the sail hangs slack or the tiller swings hard, and a rare quiet plank creak under way. A boat at rest is silent, and the sounds follow the Ambience volume slider.
entries.publicSummary: Added boat sounds at the helm: rushing water that follows your speed, sail flutter and an occasional creak.

entries.text: On a server, a queued craft the server refused only for arriving too soon now goes back to the front of the queue and is sent again ('Server busy | retrying … x n, materials kept'), up to three times in a row, instead of being dropped.
entries.publicSummary: Fixed queued crafts on a server being dropped when the server was briefly busy.

entries.text: In Creative, middle-click copies a door's exact style, wood and size, and Shift+left-click locks a whole closed door to move: aim at clear, supported ground, press R to turn the preview and right-click to place. Left click or B cancels; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo the move. On a hosted Creative world the server confirms the lock, move and each Undo/Redo.
entries.publicSummary: Added moving whole closed doors in Creative, with undo and redo, also on servers. Middle-click copies a door's style, wood and size.

entries.text: Tables placed edge to edge with matching woods and floor height now join into one dining table on any side, including L, T and wider shapes; shared legs and rails disappear while each piece stays separate. A new Desk plan (1.5 by 0.75 m) joins end to end in a straight line. Changes that would push returning legs into blocks, furniture or players are refused.
entries.publicSummary: Added joining tables into larger dining tables, and a writing desk that joins end to end.

entries.text: New storage furniture: the Wardrobe (two doors) and Chest of drawers (three drawers), each with Body, Front and Fittings woods; an open Bookcase with private storage that can also hold a red lantern on top; and a Wall shelf that hangs on two solid wall pieces and can display a red lantern. Storage holds 250 capacity and 64 kinds of item, and pieces must be emptied before taking them up.
entries.publicSummary: Added wardrobes, chests of drawers and a bookcase to store things in, and a wall shelf. Bookcases and shelves can show a red lantern.

entries.text: While storage is open, wardrobe and kitchen cupboard doors swing open and the top drawer of a chest of drawers slides out on your own screen, if the space in front is clear; Reduce motion shows them open at once. Kitchen cupboards and wall cupboards gain a separate Fittings choice for the handle wood, costing one more board.
entries.publicSummary: Changed wardrobe and cupboard doors to swing open, and the top drawer to slide out, while you use their storage. Cupboard handles can have their own wood.

entries.text: Carry a furniture hammer, aim at a placed wooden chest and press E to Refinish chest: choose body, lid and fittings woods and Apply. The contents stay inside, Survival spends only the boards (four body, three lid, one fittings), and Ctrl+Z restores the old chest. On a server the editor first reads the chest, and Apply, Undo and Redo wait for the server.
entries.publicSummary: Added refinishing wooden chests with the furniture hammer. Choose new woods for the body, lid and fittings without emptying the chest.

entries.text: On servers you can now put a red lantern on a table and take it back, with Undo and Redo; the server confirms your stock and no hammer is needed. Moving or turning a table carries its lantern, solo and online. Creative players on a server can also undo and redo furniture material changes.
entries.publicSummary: Added putting lanterns on tables on servers, with undo and redo. Tables can now be moved with a lantern on them.

entries.text: In solo worlds, chest placement, item transfers, take-up and opening an old chest are checked against the 8 MiB world-file limit before anything changes, so an action that would make the save too big is refused and items stay where they were.
entries.publicSummary: Fixed chest actions near the save size limit. An action that would make the world file too big is now refused before any items move.

If a save fails, the action keeps waiting until a later save works.
entries.publicSummary: Fixed dedicated servers confirming item, crafting, food, combat and building actions before they had been saved.

entries.text: Hosted and dedicated servers check the complete world file before item transfers, drops and pickups, crafting, water flask exchanges, melee, ranged and blast loot and egg hatches. entries.publicSummary: Fixed servers near the save size limit. Actions that would make the world file too big are now refused and keep your items.

entries.publicSummary: Added a washbasin, a toilet you can sit on and a bathtub, in clay, stone, marble or iron.
